entries.title: Arnold von Uissigheim
entries.english:
Arnold III von Uissigheim also blessed Arnold and King Armleder (executed 14 November 1336) was a medieval German highwayman, bandit, and renegade knight of the Uissigheim family, of the village Uissigheim of the same name. He was the leader of the "Armleder" massacres against Jewish communities throughout the Alsace in 1336.
Arnold became a wanted man in 1332 on the charge of highway robbery in the Wertheim territorium. He then commenced a wave of populist banditry and massacres against the Jewish population of the Alsace. Arnold and 47 of his band were taken captive in 1336, and Arnold tried and sentenced to death by the Zentgericht court.

"In 1334, Jews were killed in the town of Röttingen, AUB, Bischofsheim and many other towns and villages. Author and instigator of this persecution was a certain Knight of Uissinkeim. Affiliated Jews prompted the Mr Gottfried von Hohenlohe by a gift of 400 pounds Heller, to catch the Knight. He was picked up and taken to Röttingen. There, he repeatedly filed the confession to the Dean and was permitted to receive the sacraments. He was eventually led to the city of Kitzingen and there beheaded. The body brought in his village of Uissigheim and buried them in the Church. There he became known by countless miracles." According to the (now lost) inscription to the tombstone, Knight Arnold was beheaded with his own sword, what to look at is as a special benefit, as well as the burial in consecrated ground. The legend claims the Knight was murdered by Jews, was only added at a later time."

entries.title: Boxberg
entries.english:
Castle Boxberg is located on a mountain spur above the village of the same name and the river Umpfer. Not much of the castle is now preserved. It is assumed that Boxberg consisted of a double ditch with a double drawbridge, as well as a circumferential kennel and several defensive towers. The complex resembled a fortress before it was destroyed. A copperplate engraving from 1645 shows the castle in full.
Today, only a few remains of the once large complex are encountered. Clearly visible and accessible are the old casemates, which were housed in a natural rock, which carried the shield wall to the east. In front of the casemates, the fountain was again exposed, which was located in the middle of the inner castle. The houses of rule in the west are no longer existent. They replaced a large meadow, which no longer has a trace of buildings. Own mountain formations make it difficult to understand the course of the building complex.
The outer weir can still be clearly seen. In the southwest a tower with surrounding clamping walls was rebuilt. From him runs the ditch, which at the same time served as a kennel, around the inner castle. It still sets itself apart from the surrounding forest floor today and reveals the dimensions that he and thus the outer border of the castle area once had. To the east are the remains of two defensive towers, most of which were cut out of the natural rock. They can still be viewed today and walk through the old rises.
Despite their poor preservation, the overgrown and completely disappeared Boxberg Castle houses numerous small things and details that are difficult to recognize and assign.

The first castle dates from the 11th. century. The second complex was built on the foundations of the first around 1480 and was destroyed in 1523. The third castle was from 1547 to 1857. It was then completely broken off. Today there are only a few remnants left.

On the 23rd On 1 January 1470, Mainz, Würzburg and the Electoral Palatinate joined forces to form an alliance against the Rosenbergers. With a force of 200 footknechtes and 300 horsemen, they took action against Boxberg Castle with a crew of 120 men armed with rifles. The accusation of the robber baron gave rise, but the territorial interests also played a major role. In 1486, he moved against the Würzburg Bishop Rudolf II of Scherenberg in Fehde, whom he considered to be the main responsible of the distress.

As helpers of Hans Thomas von Absberg and through their own Rosenberg feud, the Rosenbergs came under pressure again in 1523 during the Franconian War, this time through the Swabian League. He arrived with an overpowering army to stop the robber barrily and destroyed several castles of the Rosenbergers. The Wandereisen woodcuts from 1523 describe the train of the covenant, which fought the Rosenberg Castle Boxberg, the town of Aub, Waldmannshofen Castle, Gnötzheim Castle and the Dietenhofen water castle.
The Boxberger line of the Rosenbergers became extinct in 1542

entries.german: Uissigheim

Grabplatte in der Kirche an der Westwand, zum größten Teil durch einen Kirchenstuhl verdeckt und stark überstrichen. Sandstein, etwa 220 × 100, Schrift 6 cm. Das Mittelfeld zeigt in flachem Relief den Uissigheimer Schild mit Helm und Zimier. Von der linken Schriftleiste fehlen die oberen zwei Drittel aller Buchstaben.
entries.english: Grave slab in the church on the west wall, for the most part covered by a church pew and heavily painted over. Sandstone, approximately 220x100 cm, script 6 cm. The central panel shows in low relief the Uissigheim shield with helmet and crest. From the left inscription band, the upper two-thirds of all letters are missing.

entries.german: Gamans (siehe Nr. 92) überliefert: † anno dni m · ccc · xxxii obiit Ebirhardus de Ussenken · bone · memorie · qui · dicebatur · der · anneberc · I · K · Januarii. Severus schreibt bei einer davon unabhängigen zweiten Wiedergabe des Wortlautes: eberhardus und de ranneberg.
entries.english: Gamans (see No. 92) records: † In the year of the Lord 1332 died Eberhardus de Ussenken of good memory, who was called 'der anneberc', on the day before the Kalends of January. Severus, in a second, independent record of the wording, writes: eberhardus und de ranneberg.

entries.german: 1332 starb Eberhard von Uissigheim seligen Angedenkens, der von Ranneberg genannt wurde.
entries.english: In 1332 died Eberhard von Uissigheim of blessed memory, who was called von Ranneberg.

entries.german: Nach Werr ist er nachweisbar in Bronnbacher Urkunden von 1323 zusammen mit Ritter Arnold (Nr. 109?), 1328 und 1330 allein, stets mit dem Zusatz „von Ranneberg“, unter dem wohl die heute verschwundene Randenburg bei Alzenau zu verstehen ist¹.
entries.english: According to Werr, he is verifiable in Bronnbach charters from 1323 together with Knight Arnold (No. 109?), [and in] 1328 and 1330 alone, always with the addendum "von Ranneberg," by which the now-vanished Randenburg castle near Alzenau is probably to be understood¹.

entries.german: Bronnbach

Grabplatte im Kreuzgang an der Westwand. Br. Z. 35; g. S. 193 × 78, Schrift 6,5–8,5 cm. Stark abgetretene Umrißzeichnung einer Frauengestalt mit Umschrift, links und rechts vom Kopf das Rosenberger und Tottenheimer Wappen. Die Ränder verschiedentlich ausgebessert.
1418 am Mittwoch (18. Mai) nach Pfingsten starb Margaretha von Rosenberg.

Zwischen „post“ und „penthecoste“ ein freier Raum von etwa fünf Buchstaben. Der Stein wird wohl schon beim Anbringen der Umschrift an dieser Stelle beschädigt gewesen sein (ähnlich bei Nr. 132). – Margaretha ist als Frau des Hans von Dottenheim (Nr. 135) bezeugt¹.
Margaretha von Rosenberg † 1418.
Grosse Platte (r. S.) mit Resten einer eingeritzten weiblichen Figur; rechts neben dem Kopf ein (jetzt) leerer, links der Tottenheimer (Widder) Wappenschild.
Die Umschrift lautet:
Im liber mortuorum zum 19. Mai 1418 richtig verzeichnet. Zwischen »post« und »pentecoste« ist in der Inschrift ein Absatz, wahrscheinlich weil der Stein dort von vornherein etwas beschädigt war.
Wölchingen

Grabstein in der Kirche an der Südwand. Gelber Sandstein 222x102, Schrift 9–11 cm. Über der Platte noch ein nicht dazu gehöriger rechteckiger Aufsatz mit dem Cronberger Wappen. Die Umschrift beginnt links unten. Die Wappen bedeuten links Rosenberg, rechts Dörzbach(?). Datum: 16. Juni. – Die Inschrift ist in unserem Bezirk die älteste Grabinschrift in deutscher Sprache; nur die Gründungsinschrift Nr. 5 ist noch älter. – Eberhard kaufte 1381 mit seinem Bruder Arnold und zwei Rosenbergern einer anderen Linie vom verschuldeten Johanniterorden Burg und Stadt Boxberg; jeder erhielt ein Viertel der Herrschaft. Die Brüder trugen ihre Hälfte noch am gleichen Tag dem Pfalzgrafen zu Lehen auf. Als Arnold Teil an Schüpf erworben hatte, verkaufte er 1387 sein Viertel an seinen Bruder. Im selben Jahr noch starb Eberhard eines gewaltsamen Todes; durch Zugeständnisse in Zehntstreitigkeiten erwirkten seine Söhne Arnold (Nr. 144) und Eberhard (Nr. 145) vom Würzburger Bischof das kirchliche Begräbnis. Seine Gemahlin war Else von Erligheim.
entries.english: Tombstone in the church on the south wall. Yellow sandstone 222x102 cm, script 9–11 cm. Above the slab is a non-original rectangular attachment with the Cronberg coat of arms. The inscription begins at the bottom left. The coats of arms signify Rosenberg on the left, Dörzbach(?) on the right. ✠ In the year of the Lord 1387, on the next Sunday after St. Vitus' Day, died Lord Eberhard von Rosenberg Date: June 16 – The inscription is the oldest tomb inscription in the German language in our district; only the founding inscription No. 5 is older. – In 1381, Eberhard, with his brother Arnold and two Rosenbergs from another line, bought the castle and town of Boxberg from the indebted Order of St. John; each received a quarter of the lordship. The brothers transferred their half as a fief to the Count Palatine on the same day. After Arnold had acquired a part of Schüpf, he sold his quarter to his brother in 1387. In the same year, Eberhard died a violent death; through concessions in tithing disputes, his sons Arnold (No. 144) and Eberhard (No. 145) obtained a church burial from the Bishop of Würzburg. His wife was Else von Erligheim.

entries.title: Grave of Eberhard
entries.german: Grabstein (w. S.) des Eberhard von Rosenberg († 1387) mit der Freifigur (vergl. 1. und 2.) des Ritters in voller Rüstung. Die Füsse ruhen auf einer schrägen Platte, Haltung wie bei 1. Die Umschrift lautet:  ✿ Anno· dni· m ccc· lxxxvii·iar· an· dem· neſten· ſuntag· noch· vity· ſtarp· her· eeb’hart· von· roſenberg. In Technik und Auffassung mit 1. verwandt und wiederum von einem nicht dazu ge- hörigen Wappenschild bekrönt. Die gothische Minuskel auf diesem Steine besonders schön gehauen. Nur ist dem Bildhauer das Missgeschick passirt, dass er bei dem Vor- namen des Ritters zwei e hintereinander angebracht hat.
entries.english: Tombstone (west side) of Eberhard von Rosenberg († 1387), featuring a free-standing figure (see nos. 1 and 2) of the knight in full armor. His feet rest on a slanted slab, positioned as in example 1. The inscription reads: ✿ *In the year of our Lord 1387, on the next Sunday after Pentecost, died Lord Eberhard von Rosenberg.* [3 June 1387 (Julian) \= 11 June 1387 (Gregorian)] [for them it would be 15 june, because it's 50 days after Easter (pentecost)] In terms of technique and style, it is related to example 1, and once again topped by a heraldic shield that does not belong to it. The Gothic minuscule script on this stone is particularly well carved. Only, the sculptor made the mistake of placing two r’s in a row in the knight’s first name.

entries.title: Hofmann, “Die romanische Kirche in Boxberg-Wölchingen” (Neues Archiv f. d. Geschichte d. Stadt Heidelberg, Bd. 8, 1910, pp. 133)
entries.german: Die übrigen Denkmäler im Innern der Kirche stehen alle auf- recht an den Wänden der beiden Seitenschiffe , wohin sie im Jahre 1877 verbracht wurden . Das älteste von diesen Grabmälern im nördlichen Seitenschiff ist dem Ritter Eberhard von Rosenberg errichtet , der im Jahre 1387 starb . Es ist aus weißem Sandstein und trägt in gotischen Buchstaben die Umschrift : Anno dni mccclxxxvii jar an dem nehsten suntag nach vity starp her eebhart von rosen- berg . Der Ritter in Lebensgröße und voller Rüstung auf einer ab- geschrägten Platte stehend ist in beinahe völlig herausgearbeiteter Figur dargestellt . Beide Arme hängen herab ; die linke Hand liegt an dem Griff des langen Ritterschwertes , während die rechte das Halbschwert , den Dolchgriff , umfaßt hält . Oben links in der Ecke ist das Rosenbergische , links ein unbekanntes Wappenschild , beide in gotischer Form . Das Gesicht des Ritters zeigt individuelle Züge , die ganze Figur ist sehr sorgfältig ausgearbeitet und stammt aus der Werkstätte eines unbekannten , aber tüchtigen Bildhauers . Über dem Denkmal steht ein Rosenbergisches Wappen mit Schwanenhälsen als Helmzier und dazwischen eine fünfblätterige Rose . Dieser Eber- hard von Rosenberg ist der Gemahl der schon erwähnten Els von Erlikheim . Nach einer Urkunde ( General - Landesarchiv in Karlsruhe ) vom 22. Juni 1337 gestattete der Bischof von Würzburg das kirch- liche Begräbnis des von seinen Feinden umgebrachten Eberhard von Rosenberg , nachdem dessen Erben sich über ihre Ansprüche auf die strittigen Zehnten zu Wölchingen mit dem Bischof verständigt hatten .
entries.english: The remaining monuments inside the church all stand upright against the walls of the two side aisles, where they were moved in 1877. The oldest of these tombs, in the north aisle, is that of the knight Eberhard von Rosenberg, who died in 1387. It is made of white sandstone and bears the inscription in Gothic script: "Anno dni mccclxxxvii jar an dem nehsten suntag nach vity starp her eebhart von rosenberg." The knight, life-size and in full armor, stands on a slanted slab and is depicted in almost completely sculpted form. Both arms hang down; the left hand rests on the hilt of the long knight's sword, while the right grasps the half-sword, the dagger hilt. In the upper left corner is the Rosenberg coat of arms, and to the left an unknown one, both in Gothic style. The knight's face displays individual features; the entire figure is very carefully crafted and originates from the workshop of an unknown but skilled sculptor. Above the monument is a Rosenberg coat of arms with swan necks as a crest and a five-petaled rose between them. This Eberhard von Rosenberg is the husband of the aforementioned Els von Erlikheim. According to a document (General State Archives in Karlsruhe) dated June 22, 1337, the Bishop of Würzburg permitted the church burial of Eberhard von Rosenberg, who had been murdered by his enemies, after his heirs had reached an agreement with the bishop regarding their claims to the disputed tithes in Wölchingen.

entries.title: unknown
entries.german: Unter der Kirche befindet sich eine Gruft, in welche man auf einer Wendeltreppe hinabsteigt; sie hat wie die alten Krypten ein Kreuzgewölbe. In dieser Krypta war die Grablege der Johanniter, so wie der jeweiligen Besitzer von Boxberg. Drei Grabmale beurkunden, daß letztere in späterer Zeit hier ihr Begräbniß hatten. Das älteste Grabmal steht sechs Fuß vom Altar am Eckpfeiler und stellt in erhabener Arbeit einen gewaltigen Ritter dar mit Helm, Ringkragen, Ringhosen und bauschigten Aermeln, der auf einem Löwen steht. Die Inschrift in eckiger Mönchsschrift lautet: Anno domini MCCCLXXXVII. jar an dem nechsten suntag nach Vity starp her Ekkard von Rosenberg. Oben an den Ecken des Steins sind 2 Wappen sichtbar, darüber das rosenberg'sche. Gegenüber von Eckard v. Rosenberg unter der Emporkirche steht das Denkmal Arnolds v. Rosenberg. Die Ritterfigur ist mit einem Plattenharnisch  (...) Noch machen wir auf den einzigen, auf dem Boden der Kirche liegenden Grabstein aufmerksam. Gehen wir vom südlichen Portal einige Schritte gerade aus vorwärts, so stehen wir auf demselben. Der Stein ist so sehr abgetreten, daß man die beiden neben einander stehenden Wappenschilde kaum mehr erkennen kann. Was von der Inschrift noch lesbar ist, lautet also:     Anno domini MCCCXXI ... sancti Andreae apostoli Bertholdus de nova domo pide... requiescat... Von was für einem neuen Haus (nova domo) sich...
entries.english: Beneath the church there is a crypt, into which one descends via a spiral staircase; like the old crypts, it has a cross-vault. In this crypt was the burial place of the Knights of St. John, as well as that of the respective owners of Boxberg. Three tombs document that the latter had their burial here in later times. The oldest tomb stands six feet from the altar at the corner pillar and depicts in raised work a mighty knight with a helmet, mail coif, mail chausses, and puffy sleeves, who stands on a lion. The inscription in angular monastic script reads: In the year of the Lord 1387, on the next Sunday after St. Vitus' Day, died Lord Eckard von Rosenberg. At the upper corners of the stone, 2 coats of arms are visible, above them the Rosenberg one. Opposite from Eckard von Rosenberg, under the gallery, stands the monument of Arnold von Rosenberg. The figure of the knight is with a plate armor… (...) We would also like to draw attention to the only tombstone lying on the floor of the church. If we go a few steps straight ahead from the southern portal, we are standing on it. The stone is so very worn that one can hardly recognize the two adjacent coats of arms anymore. What is still legible of the inscription reads thus:     In the year of the Lord 1321 ... of Saint Andrew the apostle, Bertholdus of the new house ... may he rest... Of what kind of new house (nova domo)...

entries.title: unknown
entries.german: Ein Arnold v. Rosenberg der junge, geſesſen zu Vorberg, iſt uns a. 1394 erſtmals begegnet, als Beſiegler einer Urkunde; Reg. b. XI, 3. 1395 verkauſten Arnold v. R. der junge und Eberhard v. Rosenberg Brüder, Herrn Eberhards ſelig v. R. Söhne, eine Wieſe in Kupſrich- hauſen an die Martine. Schon die Wiederkehr des Namens Arnold macht es hier wahrſcheinlich, daß wir Angehörige desſelben Familien- zweigs vor uns haben. Wir glauben desweſen auch, daß der Vater Eberhard jener C. v. R., Ritter, geweſen iſt, welcher in einer Ur- kunde von 1385 „Vogt zu Lauda“ heißt, aber ſchon am 15. Juni 1388 geſtorben iſt, wie im Necrolog Jahresheft 1861 eingeſchrieben ſteht: *Eberhardus de R. miles*. Sein wird wohl das Grabdenk- mal zu Wölchingen ſein, welches Schönnhuth wahrſcheinlich ungenau beſchreibt mit der Inſchrift: *A. D. MCCCLXXXVII jar an dem nechſten Suntag nach Vity (15. Juni) ſtarp her Ettard v. Roſenberg.* — Nach einer handſchriftlichen Notiz ſcheint das Mutterwappen das der Herrn von Thüngen zu ſein; vgl. 1856, S. 34.
entries.english: A young Arnold von Rosenberg, residing in Vorberg, is first encountered by us in 1394 as a sealer of a document; Reg. b. XI, 3. In 1395, Arnold von R. the younger and Eberhard von Rosenberg, brothers, sons of the late Lord Eberhard von R., sold a meadow in Kuprich- hausen to the Martine. The recurrence of the name Arnold already makes it probable that we have members of the same family branch before us here. We therefore also believe that the father Eberhard was that C. von R., knight, who in a document from 1385 is called "Vogt zu Lauda," but already died on June 15, 1388, as is recorded in the Necrology Annual 1861: *Eberhardus de R. miles* (Eberhard von R., knight). His tombstone will probably be in Wölchingen, which Schönnhuth probably inaccurately describes with the inscription: *A. D. 1387, on the next Sunday after Vity (June 15), Lord Ettard von Rosenberg died.* — According to a handwritten note, the maternal coat of arms seems to be that of the Lords von Thüngen; cf. 1856, p. 34.

entries.title: About Schönau monastery
entries.german: Vor Abt Pater zu Schönau geschah die Vereinigung, nach welcher dem Caplan jener Pfründe eine ewige Gült von zwanzig Pfund Heller, „als sie zu Heidelberg genge und gebe sind“, erkauft werden solle. Dazu werden an die gestiftete Seelenmesse gesetzt 12 Malter ewiger Korngilt von des Klosters Hof zu Edingen und zwei Häuser zu Heidelberg, das eine gelegen am Berge, das andere in der Mantelgasse im Brückenried, dazu ½ Morgen Wingert in Leimheimer Mark und zwei Stückel Weingarten zu Handschuchsheim am Bruckenried, endlich drei Morgen Weingarten in Rohrbacher Gemarkung am Pleckhard und in Bergheimer Gemarkung am Geißberg und in Handschuchsheimer im Lobenfelder gelegen. Von letztern soll Pfarrer Hartlieb sein Leben lang die Nutzung haben. Die Stiftung wurde 1379 vom Abt zu Schönau, der Äbtissin und dem Pfarrer Hartlieb besiegelt und nach dem Tode der Carisina 1388 vom Wormser Bischof Eckhard von Ders bestätigt. Die Nachfolgerin Carisina's dürfte jene Äbtissin Agnes Ulnerin von Dyhpurg (Dieburg bei Darmstadt) gewesen sein, deren Grabstein im Stift ihren Todestag als den Tag nach St. Barbara (5. Dec.) des Jahres 1403*) überliefert hat. Noch zählte nach ihr das Kloster unter seinen Wohlthätern 1410 Elisabeth von Weyler, genannt Krensin, eine Klosterfrau, und 1420 die Wittwe Elisabeth von Erlickheim, geborne von Rosenberg auf.
entries.english: Before Abbot Pater of Schönau, the unification took place, according to which the chaplain of that prebend was to be bought an eternal due of twenty pounds of Heller, "as is customary and valid in Heidelberg." For this, 12 Malter¹ of perpetual grain rent from the monastery's estate at Edingen are endowed to the requiem mass, as well as two houses in Heidelberg, one situated on the hill, the other in the Mantelgasse in the Brückenried district, plus ½ Morgen² of vineyard in the Leimheim district and two small plots of vineyard at Handschuchsheim in the Bruckenried district, and finally three Morgen of vineyard in the Rohrbach district at Pleckhard and in the Bergheim district at Geißberg and located in Handschuchsheim's Lobenfeld. Of the latter, Pastor Hartlieb is to have the use for his entire life. The foundation was sealed in 1379 by the Abbot of Schönau, the abbess, and Pastor Hartlieb, and confirmed after the death of Carisina in 1388 by the Bishop of Worms, Eckhard von Ders. Carisina's successor was likely that Abbess Agnes Ulnerin von Dyhpurg (Dieburg near Darmstadt), whose tombstone in the convent has recorded her day of death as the day after St. Barbara's Day (Dec. 5th) of the year 1403. After her, the monastery still counted among its benefactors in 1410 Elisabeth von Weyler, called Krensin, a nun, and in 1420 the widow Elisabeth von Erligheim, born von Rosenberg.

entries.title: Museum
entries.english:
The two memorial stones of Jörg and Osanna of Rosenberg were originally located on the outer wall of the Boxberg Castle in the Main-Tauber-Kreis, on the side of the gate. The surrounding inscription, which began on the man's stone and interswitched to the stone of the woman, explains that the Rosenberg couple had the stones set to commemorate the completion of their castle.

The dligen Rosenbergs wear daytime clothes. Jörg Rosenberg wears a cap, a knee-short skirt and shoes, Osanna Rosenberg dress and hood. Both are equipped with objects to point out their cooperation in the construction of the castle: he shoulders a axe, carries a bottle and food in two pots set in each other in the net, plus a handle basket filled with bread for the workers. Both hold a rosary in their hands. In formal terms, the memorial stones with the chest relief and the circulating inscription follow the type of ancient gravestones. 

around 1493
Karlsruhe, Badisches Landesmuseum (castle), exhibition of late Middle Ages

entries.title: Week day
entries.english:
✿ In the year of our Lord 1387, on the next Sunday after st Vity, died Lord Eberhard von Rosenberg.
But what date is it?
15, 16, 24?
The entry refers to Sunday, 16 June 1387 (Julian), which is Sunday, 24 June 1387 on our modern Gregorian calendar.

entries.latin: Anno domini M⁰CCC⁰LXXXVII⁰ mensis Augusti die XXIII videlicet feria sexta in vigilia sancti Bartholomei in capitulo declaratum est, quod dominus Martinus canonicus dictus de Uterin debet solvere de prebenda in Pobrycz onus in anniversario vigiliae assumptionis, antequam censum percepisset. Hoc idem eciam declaratum extat observari in aliis.
entries.english:
In the year of the Lord 1387, in the month of August, on the 23rd day, namely Friday, on the vigil of Saint Bartholomew, it was declared in chapter that Lord Martin, the canon called ‘of Uterin,’ must pay from the prebend in Pobrycz the due obligation on the anniversary of the Vigil of the Assumption, before he had received the rent. This same matter is also declared to be observed likewise in other cases.
(23 August 1387, Friday)
